- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >65) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast peaks 2–3 days after a price spike, reduce that peak by 5–10%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid over-optimism in early days (1–5) — cap forecast at +5% above 14-day moving average.
- Sentiment decay effect: if sentiment drops below 0.2 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid downward drift.
